title: Exotic superconductivity in the doped Kitaev quantum spin liquid
abstract: We investigate superconductivity in a doped Kitaev quantum spin liquid by applying the many-variable variational Monte Carlo method to the hole-doped $t$-$J$-type Kitaev model. Using a projected pair-product wave function that can exactly represent the Kitaev quantum spin liquid, we examine the stability of superconducting phases on isotropic two-dimensional clusters. For the ferromagnetic Kitaev interaction, robust triplet $p$-wave superconductivity coexists with ferromagnetism in the low-to-intermediate doping regime but is suppressed as the system approaches the fully polarized ferromagnetic phase. For the antiferromagnetic Kitaev interaction, superconductivity exhibits a change in the dominant pairing symmetry from spin-dependent triplet $p$-wave at low doping to singlet $d+id$ at intermediate doping. By varying the strength of the ferromagnetic Kitaev interaction at fixed doping, we show that the triplet superconductivity increases together with the ferromagnetic moment and becomes strongest slightly below full polarization. Our results provide a theoretical basis for experimental searches for unconventional superconductivity, such as triplet superconductivity coexisting with ferromagnetism, in carrier-doped Kitaev candidate materials.
summary: The authors theoretically investigate exotic superconductivity in the doped Kitaev quantum spin liquid using variational Monte Carlo simulations. They find that superconducting pairing symmetries are highly dependent on doping and the sign of the Kitaev interaction, predicting robust triplet p-wave superconductivity coexisting with ferromagnetism for FM coupling. This work offers a theoretical roadmap for searching for such unconventional phases in real materials.
main_problem: The study investigates exotic superconducting phases, particularly triplet p-wave and singlet d+id pairing, that can coexist with ferromagnetism in a doped Kitaev quantum spin liquid.
main_result: For ferromagnetic coupling, robust triplet superconductivity coexists with ferromagnetism at low to intermediate doping. For antiferromagnetic coupling, the superconducting symmetry changes from triplet p-wave to singlet d+id pairing as doping increases.
method: The research employs the many-variable variational Monte Carlo (mVMC) method using a projected pair-product wave function representation of the Kitaev quantum spin liquid.
model_or_system: The system is the hole-doped t-J-type Kitaev model on the honeycomb lattice, analyzed for both ferromagnetic ($K/t=-1$) and antiferromagnetic ($K/t=+1$) Kitaev interactions. The analysis covers doping regimes ($\delta$).
key_observables: Superconducting pairing correlations (singlet/triplet), uniform magnetization per site ($M_\alpha$), and total magnetization ($M_{all}$).
important_parameters: Doping concentration ($\delta$), Kitaev interaction strength ratio ($K/t$), and lattice size ($L=8, 10, 12$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on projecting the BCS state onto a fixed particle number sector to obtain the pair-product wave function $|\phi_{	ext{pair}}(F)angle$. The fate in the thermodynamic limit remains an open question.
figures_summary: Figures show phase diagrams vs. doping for FM/AFM cases, distance dependence of pairing correlations ($D_{\eta}^\alpha(r)$), and doping dependence of triplet correlation ($P_{all}^{py}$) alongside total magnetization ($M_{all}$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the superconducting ground state by first establishing the theoretical framework using projected wave functions (BdG approach) and then applying mVMC to calculate pairing correlations and magnetization across different doping regimes for both FM and AFM couplings.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses unconventional superconductivity in a highly correlated magnetic system, providing concrete predictions—like triplet p-wave coexistence with magnetism—that guide experimental searches in candidate materials.
